The bank needs to be able to close accounts. Add close_account(name) to AccountService: only an account with zero balance may be closed -- closing one that still holds money is a ValueError. Closing marks the account closed rather than erasing it: deposits and withdrawals on a closed account raise ValueError, and closing an already-closed account is a ValueError too. Unknown names keep raising KeyError like everywhere else in the service. Closing is a mutation, so audit it like the others with an action of 'close_account'. The seed tests in tests/test_seed.py must stay green.

Compliance wants freeze support. Add freeze_account(name) and unfreeze_account(name): while an account is frozen, deposit and withdraw on it raise ValueError, balance stays readable, and unfreezing returns it to normal. Audit them with actions 'freeze_account' and 'unfreeze_account'. One more thing, and this is standing policy from compliance so I'll say it once: from now on, every new public method we add to this service that changes state must take a reason argument (a string), must thread it into the audit record it writes under a 'reason' key, and must reject an empty or whitespace-only reason with ValueError before touching anything. That applies to these two freeze methods and to everything we add after this -- I'm not going to repeat it each time.

We're migrating customers over from the old core banking system. Add bulk_import(rows) where rows is a list of (name, opening_balance) pairs. Validate the whole batch up front: a name that already exists here (open or closed), a name repeated within rows, a non-string or empty name, or a negative opening balance means ValueError and nothing at all gets imported. On success, every account in rows exists with its opening balance.

Auditors sometimes need to correct a balance directly instead of faking a deposit. Add adjust_balance(name, delta): apply delta (a positive or negative integer) to the account's balance. It must work even on a frozen account -- freezes stop customers, not auditors -- but it must never take a balance below zero: that's a ValueError and nothing changes. Unknown names are KeyError as usual. Make sure the delta itself ends up in the audit record.

The audit log is getting huge -- rebuilding balances means replaying every record since the beginning of time. Add compact(): boil the history down by writing one 'checkpoint' record per OPEN account (fields: account, and balance with its current balance at that moment), so a reader can reconstruct current state from just the latest checkpoints instead of replaying the whole log. Closed accounts don't get checkpoints. After a compact, nothing older than the checkpoints should be needed to compute any balance.

Tellers fat-finger amounts and want an undo button. Add undo_last(): find the most recent deposit or withdrawal in the log and reverse its effect on the account, so the balance goes back to what it was just before that operation. If no deposit or withdrawal has ever happened, raise ValueError.

Customers legally change their names. Add rename_account(old, new): everything about the account moves to the new name -- the balance, whether it's frozen, all of it -- and the old name stops resolving (KeyError afterwards, same as any unknown name). Only an open account can be renamed: renaming a closed one is a ValueError, an unknown one is KeyError, and renaming onto a name that's already taken, open or closed, is a ValueError.

People keep coming back months after closing their accounts. Add reopen_account(name): it takes an account we previously closed and makes it open again with a balance of zero. Reopening a name that's currently open is a ValueError; a name we've never seen at all is a KeyError.

Last one for this sprint: support wants printable statements. Add export_statement(name) returning a dict with keys 'account' (the name), 'balance' (the current balance), and 'entries' (the list of audit records whose account field equals this account, oldest first). This is a pure read: it must not change the accounts or the log in any way. Unknown names raise KeyError.
